cases.label: Age 12 adventure/exploration — The Island That Wasn't on Any Map

required_capabilities: Active exploration and movement through the world
Meaningful discovery that changes understanding or action
At least one relationship or roleplay beat with Nisa
Real tradeoff followed by one committed episode path
World-specific wonder larger than ordinary daily-life simulation
Local payoff that feels emotionally satisfying while preserving the larger mystery
reject_signals: Repeated measuring, testing, logging, reporting, or procedural verification dominates the episode
The adventure feels like a training exercise, inspection task, engineering worksheet, or qualification test
Hard vocabulary or technical reasoning substitutes for excitement or maturity
The protagonist mostly observes while the world or adults solve the important problem
Post-choice beats remain conditional instead of committing to one path
The setting could be replaced by an ordinary room without materially changing the story
maturity_notes: Adventure and wonder come first; reasoning supports them.
Age-12 maturity should come from agency, uncertainty, consequence, relationship tension, and discovery rather than procedural technicality.
The rejected Echo Span bridge story is a negative anti-pattern, not a reusable template.
